cases.title: The skateboarding dog

item.description: A video shows a bulldog riding a skateboard down a ramp at a park, then turning to dodge a bench.

clues.A: An account called @bruno_rides. It started posting two months ago.
clues.B: A few accounts reposted it. One of them says "this is so fake lol" but doesn't say why.
clues.C: The dog's shadow goes a little blurry when he turns.
clues.D: The caption says "Day 41. He still won't turn left."
clues.E: Someone asks which park this is. The account names it and posts a second video of the same ride from another angle, with people walking past.

cases.lesson: A new account and a "fake" comment aren't proof. A second angle of the same moment is very hard to fake.

fib.right: Ugh. I hoped that blurry shadow would scare you off.
fib.wrong: Ha! That dog is real. One reply showed the same ride from another angle!

cases.title: The shark on the highway

item.description: During a real flood, a photo shows a shark swimming along a flooded highway.

clues.A: An account with 200,000 followers that posts storm photos. Most of its photos credit the photographer. This one doesn't.
clues.B: Two news sites shared it. Both link back to that same post and nothing else.
clues.C: The ripples around the fin look right, and the shark is sharp and clear.
clues.D: The caption names the city and the date of the flood. Both are correct.
clues.E: Someone asks who took it. The account replies "a follower sent it in" and won't say who.

cases.verdictNote: AI. The flood was real. The shark was not.
cases.lesson: Lots of shares can all lead back to one source. A real event doesn't make every photo of it real.

fib.right: Fine. Two news sites, one source. You spotted it.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! Both news sites just copied my post. Nobody actually saw a shark.

cases.title: The book summary

item.description: A study website has a summary of the book your class just finished. It is well written and gets the ending right.

clues.A: The summary is signed "The Study Team."
clues.B: Other summaries online tell the same main story.
clues.C: The spelling and grammar are perfect.
clues.D: It says the main character's sister helps her escape. In the book, it's her best friend who helps. She has no sister.
clues.E: You send the site a question about who wrote it. You get an instant reply that doesn't answer your question.
clues.F: No label on the summary. The site's About page says it "uses the latest technology."

cases.lesson: AI can get most things right and invent one detail with total confidence. Check details against the real thing.

fib.right: Rats. I thought nobody would notice one little sister.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! She doesn't have a sister. You read the book!

cases.title: The dragon painting

item.description: A detailed digital painting of a dragon wins the school art contest. Some students say it is too good for a 7th grader.

clues.B: An image search finds nothing like it online.
clues.C: The scales are perfectly even, and the lighting looks professional.
clues.D: In the corner, the dragon guards a goldfish bowl labeled "Bubbles." Maya's little brother has a goldfish called Bubbles.
clues.E: You ask how she made it. She opens her art app. The file has 62 layers, with a rough pencil sketch at the bottom.

cases.lesson: Being very good isn't proof of AI. The steps behind the work are.

fib.right: Bah. I was sure "too good to be real" would fool you.
fib.wrong: Ha! Maya painted it herself. Sixty-two layers, and you never asked to see them!

cases.title: The cousin's voice message

item.description: A voice message sounds exactly like your cousin. He says his phone broke and asks you to text him your mom's number on this new one.

clues.A: It came from a number you don't recognize. He says he's borrowing a friend's phone.
clues.B: Your cousin posted from his usual account an hour ago.
clues.C: The voice, the laugh, everything sounds just like him.
clues.D: He mentions your dog, Pepper, by name.
clues.E: You reply "what did we eat at Grandma's last weekend?" He answers "haha can't talk, just send it."

cases.lesson: Voices can be copied and names can be found online. Ask something only the real person would know, check through a way you already trust, and tell an adult.

fib.right: Ugh. One question only the real cousin could answer, and my plan falls apart.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! That was a copied voice. Pepper's name is all over your family's photos.

cases.title: The three hearts

item.description: A post in a homework group says: "Fun fact: an octopus has three hearts and blue blood."

clues.A: A student from another school. You don't know her.
clues.B: A science encyclopedia and the city aquarium's website both say the same thing.
clues.D: The post doesn't say where the fact comes from.
clues.E: Someone asks why three. She replies that two hearts pump blood to the gills and one pumps it to the rest of the body. She saw it on a class trip.

cases.verdictNote: Person. The fact is true, blue blood and all.
cases.lesson: Weird doesn't mean fake. Check a source you trust before you decide.

fib.right: Hmph. I thought blue blood would sound made up enough.
fib.wrong: Ha! It's true, blue blood and all. One look in an encyclopedia would have told you.

cases.title: The purple sunset

item.description: A photo shows a bright purple and orange sky over the beach.

clues.A: A photography account you don't follow. It has posted beach photos for six years.
clues.B: That evening the local weather page posted about "unusual purple skies after the storm."
clues.C: The colors look too bright to be real.
clues.D: The caption names the beach and says "right after the storm, around 7:40."
clues.E: Someone asks if it's edited. The account says "I turned the colors up a little."

cases.verdictNote: Person. It's a real photo, edited a little.
cases.lesson: Edited isn't the same as made by AI. Other witnesses are evidence.

fib.right: Fine. Edited isn't the same as AI-made. Half the town saw that sky.
fib.wrong: Ha! A real sunset with the colors turned up. Editing a photo doesn't make it AI!

cases.title: The friendly homework helper

item.description: A chat box on a homework website is called "Sam." Sam says, "I totally get it! I had the same problem in 6th grade."

clues.A: The website says Sam is "part of our tutoring team."
clues.B: The site's team page has a photo of a smiling "Sam, tutor."
clues.C: Sam replies within a second, every time, with long answers.
clues.D: Sam says it had the same problem in 6th grade but can't say which school or who the teacher was.
clues.E: You ask Sam the same math question twice. You get two different answers, both said with total confidence.
clues.F: The site's terms page, three clicks deep, mentions "automated tutoring."

cases.lesson: AI can sound like a friend and come with a friendly face. It's fine to use, as long as you know what it is.

fib.right: Bah. I gave Sam a photo and everything.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! Sam's an AI helper. The photo was just a photo.

cases.title: The four-star review

item.description: A review of a new game says: "Loved the forest level and the soundtrack. The controls took a while to get used to, but it's worth it. 4 stars."

clues.A: The account has reviewed 50 things this month, including games, blenders, shoes and a lawnmower.
clues.B: Reviews of three other games use the same line: "took a while to get used to, but it's worth it."
clues.C: It includes a small complaint, so it sounds honest.
clues.D: It mentions the forest level. The game has one, and it's shown in the trailer.
clues.E: Someone asks what the boss at the end of the forest level is like. No reply.

cases.lesson: A small complaint and one real detail can be faked too. Check what else the account has written.

fib.right: Rats. I even added a complaint to make it sound real.
fib.wrong: Gotcha! Everything in that review was in the trailer. Fifty reviews in a month, and you trusted it.

cases.title: The hamster poem

item.description: Your friend Leo shows you a poem about his hamster. It rhymes perfectly, and it is really good.

clues.A: Leo showed it to you himself at lunch.
clues.C: No spelling mistakes, and every line has the same beat.
clues.D: It's about his hamster Biscuit escaping behind the fridge last week. He told you about that when it happened.
clues.E: You ask which line was hardest. He shows you his notebook, full of crossed-out tries at rhyming "fridge."

cases.lesson: Good writing isn't proof of AI, and personal details can be typed into AI. Seeing the work in progress is the strongest proof.

fib.right: Hmph. I thought a perfect poem would make you suspicious.
fib.wrong: Ha! Leo wrote it. His crossed-out lines were right there in the notebook!
